item.description:
• Menu bar quick controls: open a file picker with ⇧⌘O, and adjust clipboard behavior inline — On Copy mode (Compress / Convert / Compress & Convert), Target Format, and Auto-Copy Result are now nested under the Optimize Clipboard toggle and stay in sync with Settings.
  • Fixed an infinite loop where Auto-Copy would re-process the file Picmal had just placed on the clipboard, stacking overlay entries and re-running compression.
  • Fixed `.jpeg` files producing a sibling `.jpg` instead of overwriting (or preserving the source extension) on both compress and convert. Same-format operations now keep the input's on-disk extension, so `.jpeg`, `.tif`, and similar aliases stay consistent.
• Redesigned the Settings window from the ground up for a cleaner, more native macOS feel.

• Rename output files using EXIF metadata with a filename pattern. Supported tokens: {original}, {date}, {datetime}, {year}, {month}, {day}, {camera}, {iso}.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Polish the watermark section and resolve some visual issues.
  • Increase the speed of image conversion.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Burn-in subtitles for video. Attach an SRT or VTT file to any video from the new film icon next to its name and the text is burned directly into the output. Style it in Settings → Video (size, color, top/center/bottom).
  • Playback speed per video. Same film icon now lets you pick 0.25×, 0.5×, 2×, 4× or a custom percentage (10–800%). Audio keeps its natural pitch. "Apply speed to all videos" copies the setting to every video in your batch.
  • Image and video watermarks. Add a logo or PNG overlay to any image or video conversion, save multiple watermark presets, and pick position (9 anchors), margins and opacity from Settings → Watermark.
  • Fixed resize settings being ignored in the Compress procedure. Max Dimensions, Max Width/Height and other resize modes now apply to compressed images, matching the Convert procedure.

• Redesigned the Settings window.
  • License activation errors now include guidance and a link to the deactivation docs when a license is already active on another device.
  • Clipboard optimization now lets you choose what happens when you copy an image: compress, convert to a different format (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF or GIF), or both.

• Fixed conversions hanging indefinitely (stuck at 99% or 0%) when batch-converting many files at once.
  • Fixed high CPU usage after conversions finish.
  • Overwrite warnings: a warning icon now appears in the convert table when a same-format conversion would overwrite the original, and in the compress bottom bar when compression prefix/suffix are empty. The Output settings page also shows per-section warnings.
  • Error output is now captured for JPEG compression failures to aid diagnostics.
  • The automatic "_converted" suffix for same-format conversions has been removed; use prefix/suffix settings instead.

• Audio files can now be converted to the same format (e.g. FLAC → FLAC) to change sample rate without switching codec.
  • New sample rate setting in Audio > Custom preset: resample audio to 8 kHz, 11.025 kHz, 16 kHz, 22.05 kHz, 32 kHz, 44.1 kHz (CD), 48 kHz (DVD), 88.2 kHz or 96 kHz.
  • Same-format conversions now automatically add a "_converted" suffix to prevent overwriting the original file.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.
• Converting MP4 to GIF fixed.

• The app now detects corrupted video files (like ones missing the moov atom) and lets you know clearly instead of failing without explanation.
  • Faster launch time. The app no longer blocks on non-essential setup before showing the first screen.
  • Cancelling a conversion feels smoother and no longer causes a brief UI freeze.
  • Fixed some concurrency issues in the background (ServiceHandler, SharedTempFileManager, and FFmpegConverter).
  • Replaced system notifications with a more integrated progress overlay that animates from the MacBook notch or slides down on other displays.
  • The menu bar icon now shows live progress percentages.
  • Improved the error interface to make issues easier to understand.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Fixed JPEG compression silently producing corrupted (truncated) output.
  • Fixed high CPU usage when idle caused by aggressive clipboard polling, always-on cache timers, broad UserDefaults observation, and unbatched FSEvents handling.
  • Watched folders now support per-folder resize settings and a "compress after convert" option.
  • New auto-copy option for clipboard optimization: compressed images are automatically copied back to the clipboard, skipping the manual "Copy" button click. Off by default.
  • Video compression now lets you change the output container format (e.g. MOV → MP4, MKV, WebM, AVI) with automatic codec compatibility handling.

• Before / After Preview — Click the eye icon on any processed file to compare original and output images with an interactive slider.
  • Video compression now offers an expanded CRF range (0–51) for finer quality control, and a new frame rate setting lets you reduce fps (e.g. 60→30) to shrink file sizes further.

• The app now remembers your last selected output format for each input type, so when you drop a new file it automatically uses the format you chose before.
  • The clipboard overlay now disappears automatically after a configurable timeout, set to 5 seconds by default, and it is no longer included in macOS screenshots.

• Improved WebP to GIF conversion. Animated WebP files now preserve all animation frames, and static WebP files convert reliably without errors.
  • New clipboard image optimization feature. Images copied to your clipboard are automatically compressed, and a compact overlay lets you quickly copy the optimized version.
  • You can now set the DPI resolution metadata on output images (72, 96, 144, 150, 300, 600 or custom) for print and display workflows — no resizing, just the metadata tag.

• Minor fixes.
  • Improved licence handling.

• New settings have been added for controlling image orientation handling and metadata preservation, with three modes: 'strip all', 'keep essential' (orientation, colour profile and copyright) or 'keep all metadata'.
  • File conversion now works reliably on iCloud Drive, network shares and read-only locations.
  • HEVC videos with unusual frame rates now convert correctly to MOV format and play properly in QuickTime.
  • Other minor improvements have been made.

• You can now drop files and folders directly into the menu tray area.
  • Fixed an issue where dragging files onto the Picmal dock icon did not work.
  • Added a few small improvements and fixes under the hood.

• Fixed an issue where the app could become unresponsive when processing complex or corrupted files.
  • Sentry error handling has been improved.
  • Made other minor fixes.
• Integrated Sentry to detect possible crashes and errors.

• The compression quality of PNG and SVG files has been improved.
  • Some crashes in macOS 14 have been fixed, especially for new users.
  • Other minor fixes.

• Clear error messages when switching between compress/convert modes.
  • The app now starts in the background when launched at login with "Keep in Menu Bar" enabled.
  • Improve images compression.
  • Fixed video compression not reducing file sizes and improved encoding performance.

• I watched folders and added hot folder monitoring.
  • You can now use Picmal with the Shortcuts app.
  • Picmal runs in the background when you log in.
  • Compress output it's available for images, audios and videos.

• Persist files when switching between the 'Convert' and 'Compress' tabs.
  • Add support for dragging and dropping files onto the dock icon.
  • Fixed an issue with SVG compression that was failing because it could not interpret some CSS classes correctly.
  • HIF format support (Canon HEIF) was added.
  • Fixed DNG/RAW rotation issue.

• Presets for audio and video conversion.
  • Support for converting HEIC to WebP.
  • You can now strip the metadata from audio, video and image files.
  • Output file displays the settings used.
  • Parts of the code have been rewritten to improve stability and reliability.
  • The Preferences menu has been reorganised for better usability.
  • Issues resulting in unusable files during MKV to MP4 conversions when certain codecs were used have been resolved.

• PDF results look clearer and sharper.
  • You can now open files from the top menu using File > Open or with the shortcut Command O.
  • Picmal now understands folders. Drop a folder and it will gather everything inside, including subfolders, ready to convert.
  • On the Finder context menu you will now see new options to convert or compress images with Picmal.

• Color space conversion: Convert images to sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Rec. 709, or Rec. 2020 with proper ICC profile embedding.
  • View color space info for converted images via a new clickable icon in the Size column.
  • Fixed FLAC to AAC audio conversion issues in optimized advanced mode.

• PDF results look clearer and sharper.
  • You can now open files from the top menu using File > Open or with the shortcut Command O.
  • Picmal now understands folders. Drop a folder and it will gather everything inside, including subfolders, ready to convert.
  • On the Finder context menu you will now see new options to convert or compress images with Picmal.

• Conversion from EPS to SVG has been added.
  • Conversion from AI to SVG added.

• PDF results look clearer and sharper.
  • You can now open files from the top menu using File > Open or with the shortcut Command O.
  • Picmal now understands folders. Drop a folder and it will gather everything inside, including subfolders, ready to convert.
  • On the Finder context menu you will now see new options to convert or compress images with Picmal.

• Color space conversion: Convert images to sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Rec. 709, or Rec. 2020 with proper ICC profile embedding.
  • View color space info for converted images via a new clickable icon in the Size column.
  • Fixed FLAC to AAC audio conversion issues in optimized advanced mode.

• Conversion from EPS to SVG has been added.
  • Conversion from AI to SVG added.

• Conversion from EPS to SVG has been added.
  • Conversion from AI to SVG added.
• Display a banner when the licence is not active to make it clear that Picmal cannot be used without a licence.

• You can now see the conversion speed percentage, along with an estimated time remaining, for videos and audio files.
  • You can now experience significant performance improvements: Video conversions are much faster and use less memory, especially for long files. Instant conversion (no re-encoding) works for 50+ format combinations including WebM, MKV, MP4, FLV, 3GP, and more.
  • You can now use VideoToolbox's H.264 hardware encoding for over 12 video formats on Apple Silicon, offering a speed boost of 10–50x for FLV, WMV, MPEG, 3GP, WTV, F4V and MXF.
  • WebM codec compatibility in Advanced mode has been fixed (now properly enforces VP8/VP9/AV1 codecs).
  • The issue where buttons (metadata, progress info, Show in Finder) were not clickable during conversion has been fixed.
  • PDF compression is now faster and more accurate.

• Fixed bug where multi-select functionality was broken for audio and video files. Format dropdown now properly populates when selecting media files via checkbox.
  • Fixed compression savings showing incorrect percentages when converting between formats.

• Fixed the non-clickable checkbox in Advanced mode.
  • Added Advanced mode to both Conversion and Compression modes.
  • Fixed the bottom tab bar so that it now truncates text when there is too much.
  • Some PDF compression errors that were not working well have been fixed.
  • Progress has been added to the compression and conversion of files to improve the user experience. Sometimes, compressing long files can take more than 2–3 minutes, and users thought it was stuck.
  • A “Cancel” button has been added while converting/compressing to allow you to stop the process.

• Batch resize images with 5 flexible modes (percentage, fixed, max
    • dimensions, width/height-only).
  • Display metadata for audio and video files (duration, bitrate, codec,
    • sample rate).
  • Advanced mode for audio and video with enhanced FFmpeg controls.
  • Fixed PDF compression corrupting colors in Keynote/PowerPoint
    • presentations.
  • Compressed files now automatically include "_compressed" suffix.
  • Improved format support (31 audio, 25 video formats).

• Support audio formats: MP3, WAV, AAC, M4A, FLAC, OGG, OGA, WMA, OPUS, M4R, AC3, WV, FSSD, AU, SPH, GSRT, CVS, CVSD, CAF, SPX, IRCAM, SND, CVU, VOC, VMS, PRC, AMB, DTS, TTA, 8SVX, DVMS, SNDR, VOX, SD2, HTK, SOU, W64, SLN, TXW, SMP, RA, SNDT, HCOM, FAP, CDDA, PAF, MAUD, MP2, WVE, NIST, AIFF, AIF, AIFC, AVR, IMA, PVF.
  • Support video formats: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WEBM, FLV, WMV, M4V, MPG, MPEG, 3GP, M2TS, MTS, VOB, ASF, OGV, WTV, TS, MJPEG, M2V, HEVC, F4V, MXF.

• 18 new formats now support conversion: JP2, PICT, QTIF, SGI, TGA, JXL, DDS, EXR, PBM, PGM, PPM, PNM,PCX, XBM, XPM, QOI, PSD.
  • 10 new formats now support compression: BMP, JP2, TGA, JXL, DDS, EXR, PCX, SGI, QOI.
• Small fixes
• Small fixes
• Fixed a crash that occurred when using the drag-and-drop view.

• Performance has been improved.
  • PDFs now convert every page, not just the first one.
  • SVG compression is now available.
  • I fixed a crash that happened when you dragged and dropped something.
  • Compression presets: You can choose from six different compression settings (maximum quality, high quality, balanced, web optimised, social media, maximum compression) or make your own custom settings.
• Enhanced conversion and compression performance.

🔐 License Activation Required

To use Picmal from this version onward, you'll need to activate your license within the app.

How to get your license key:

  1. Go to app.lemonsqueezy.com/my-orders
  2. Enter your email address
  3. Check your email for a link to access your order
  4. Copy your license key from the order page

How to activate:

  1. Open Picmal
  2. Go to Picmal → Register License…
  3. Enter your license key

Thank you for supporting Picmal!
• Small fixes and performant improvements.

• Fixed compression output: Resolved issue where files were not being compressed correctly in the output when compression settings were enabled.
  • Auto Compress Mode: Enable automatic compression on file drop! Turn on "Auto compress mode" in Preferences → Files, then simply drag files into compress mode - compression begins instantly without needing to press any buttons. Perfect for streamlined batch processing workflows.
  • Custom file naming for compression: Added prefix and suffix options for compressed output files. Configure custom naming in Preferences → Output, or leave fields blank to overwrite original files.
  • Added "Clear settings" button to reset all compression quality settings to defaults.

• New compress mode: directly reduce the size of JPG, WebP, PNG, GIF, TIFF, AVIF, and PDF files without converting them first.
  • Option to compress images after converting them to JPG, WebP, PNG, GIF, TIFF, AVIF, or PDF.
  • Minor improvements and bug fixes.

• Fix: Sometimes default format conversion was not stored properly.
  • Other small fixes.

• Added batch output format selection to apply a single format to multiple files at once.
  • Added notifications when file conversions are complete.

• Added ability to set default output formats for drag & drop. Dropped files will now automatically use these formats.
  • Introduced dark mode for a more comfortable viewing experience.
  • Improved settings menu with a cleaner and more intuitive UI.
